title: Cohort Runway & Decision Lanes — Q3 hosted API + model catalog execution play
creator: Marina Lopez
description:
Background: As usage grows and the catalog of hosted models expands, product teams need a predictable quarterly execution plan that ties model onboarding and endpoint releases to capacity commitments and clear rollback/contingency lanes. This ticket defines a cohort-driven runway and decision-lane operating model for Q3 that stitches Hosted API product commitments with the model catalog rotation schedule, canary windows, and capacity hedges.

Goals: 
- Create a single coordinated calendar (Runway) that maps cohort releases (e.g., beta customers, PLG, enterprise) to model catalog commits and reserved capacity windows.
- Define decision lanes and triggers for canary promotion, rollback, and model substitution (variant fallback) tied to SLO and quality signals.
- Surface capacity hedges and contingency slots for seasonal spikes and unexpected demand.
- Deliver a lightweight dashboard for PM/Eng/CS to track commitments, canary health, and expected token-cost impact per cohort.

Scope: Q3 hosted API + model catalog workstreams: onboarding new model tiers, rotating deprecated variants, setting canary windows for two major model swaps, and establishing capacity hedge reservations for the top 3 customer cohorts. Out of scope: Dedicated hardware procurement and deep quantization experiments (handled by ENG research workstream).

Deliverables: 
1) Quarter Runway calendar (GSheet + Epic view) with cohort lanes and pinned canary windows.
2) Decision Lanes doc: promotion/rollback triggers, automatic substitution mapping (model A -> A-lite), and escalation playbook.
3) Runway dashboard prototype in Console (read-only view for PM/CS) showing slot status, canary health, and estimated token-cost delta.
4) Stakeholder sign-offs and a scheduled canary rehearsal (dry-run) before first model swap.

Success signals: 
- All Q3 catalog releases have an assigned cohort and a canary window with owners.
- Canary promotion rules automated in orchestration config and tested in rehearsal.
- Dashboard used in weekly runway sync and reduces ad-hoc status emails by 70%.
acceptance_criteria: Quarterly runway sheet published and linked from product portal
Decision lanes doc reviewed and approved by Eng, SRE, and CS
Two canary windows scheduled with owners and pre-flight checklists
Runway dashboard prototype deployed to staging and validated with synthetic traffic
Contingency capacity slots documented and capacity hedges reserved for top 3 cohorts
